title: Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture: a finite field K of characteristic two, a finitely presented group G and a, b in K[G] with ab = 1 and ba != 1. The group is not sofic, and b defines an injective cellular automaton that is not surjective, disproving Gottschalk's conjecture. The first lesson proves stable finiteness for finite groups and, with the trace of the Kervaire course, Kaplansky's theorem in characteristic zero. The second proves the Gromov-Weiss theorem that sofic groups are surjunctive and the transfer from group algebras to automata. The third to fifth prove an incidence criterion: copies of F_l^2 glued along a line system of girth 12 embed (planar balance and Euler's formula), subgroup averages give a rectangular identity, character idempotents in a twisted extension pack it into square matrices, and matrix units of a finite group give two elements. The sixth constructs the vectors from low-degree interpolation over a field of characteristic two; the seventh to ninth construct the line system from holes, random slabs, the local lemma and local trades, and assemble the counterexample.

open_obligations: Named statements used without proof in the course, each with its exact statement and free locators in the lesson where it is stated: (LIN) Linnik's theorem on the least prime in an arithmetic progression (lesson Direction spaces and compatible holes; Linnik 1944 on Math-Net.Ru, Xylouris arXiv:0906.2749); and (PLANE) Euler's formula, facial walks and contraction of an arc for plane graphs (lesson The glued group and planar balance; Erickson's Computational Topology notes, Sections 9.4, 9.5, 10.4, 10.6; Diestel, Graph Theory, Theorem 4.2.9). A foundation course proving (PLANE) is requested from the programme coordinator; (LIN) belongs to analytic number theory.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
